title: 化学熱力学
subtitle: Chemical Thermodynamics
keywords: Physical states of substance 2.Kinetic theory of gase 3.First law of thermodynamics 4.Second law of thermodynamics 5.Enthalpy and entropy
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) Learn the physical states of substances and their roles in energy supply. (2) Research topics related to the environment and the energy supply of Hokuriku. Thermodynamics is basic to science and engineering. This course is designed to solve practical problems in chemistry using thermodynamics.
advice: This is an introductory course for materials science. We will cover the following material: 1. Basic concepts about the phases of substances 2. The behavior of atoms or molecules in gas 3. The first law of thermodynamics (including enthalpy, thermo chemistry, Hess’s law) 4. Second law of thermodynamics (including entropy and Gibbs energy, chemical changes and equilibria) 5. Introduction to statistical mechanics (concepts behind entropy) 6. Units and dimensions in science and engineering (SI system) Students are expected to bring their textbook and a scientific calculator or personal computer to every class. Students are expected to check regularly for messages/materials on the KIT Inside website, especially before every class.
books: Textbooks: Elements of Physical Chemistry; Japanese 7th edition, P. Atkins & J. Paula (Oxford University Press) Reference books: Unspecified Reserved books: Unspecified
requiredKnowledge: Basic calculation skills and a knowledge of SI units.

Be able to provide a definition of enthalpy.
Be able to explain the second law of thermodynamics.
Be able to provide a definition of entropy.

achievementLevels.ideal: (1) Apply results of gas kinetic model to the solving of problems. (2) Explain the first law and second law of thermodynamics thoroughly. (3) Correctly solve exercises in thermodynamics. (4) Apply thermodynamics appropriately for solving practical problems of society.
achievementLevels.standard: (1) Describe the kinetic model of gas. (2) Explain most of the principles of the first law and second law of thermodynamics. (3) Solve most exercises in thermodynamics correctly. (4) Apply thermodynamic principles to solve simple problems in society.
